guided_added.opener_concept: Deliver a fixed 1000 W at 10 V vs 1000 V: student computes the two currents (100 A vs 1 A) by common sense (I = P/V), revealing why the grid uses high voltage (low current = less I squared R loss) and that a transformer trades voltage for current (VpIp = VsIs).
guided_added.teach_walks: Bronze: 300:1500 turns step-up voltage. Silver: rearrange VpIp=VsIs for primary current. Gold: grid loss via I=P/V then I squared R (30 MW, 30 kV, 8 ohm -> 8 MW).
guided_added.tier_guides: Bronze one-equation turns ratio; Silver rearrange/use power; Gold chain two ideas (turns+power, efficiency, grid loss).
guided_added.guided_steps: Every numeric bank problem given micro-step walks with a phase:substitute completion boundary leaving >= 2 live boxes (compute + check). MC problems (B6/B8) omit walks.
